coverageNote: Disk enumeration matched the expected 6 units / 32 files exactly. Units: the domain directory itself (realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-index.md, -cx.md, plus the three domain-level flat features 08.06, 08.07, 08.08) and the five sub-domain directories 08.01 through 08.05, each with its own index, CX and leaf feature files. Every file was read in full through the 3a implementer-simulation / 3b rubric / 3c devil's-advocate cycle. No sampling. Rubric dimensions 2 (Persona Specificity), 4 (Constraint Explicitness), 5 (Success Measurability) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are marked N/A for all six units: personas, constraints, success metrics and competitive landscape are owned by meta/*.md and are referenced rather than redefined here (domain index line 87: 'Personas from meta/personas.md. Never redefined here — referenced only.'). That leaves dimensions 1, 3, 7 and 8 applicable to each unit — 4 checkpoints per unit, 24 total. A large number of candidate findings were dropped in 3c: this tree explicitly re-points stale deferrals ('Re-pointed from the completed /ideate-discover Step 5') roughly twenty times, and most [PENDING] markers are covered by a re-pointed, owned question elsewhere. Only markers with no owner AND no reachable stage, and contradictions with no marker on either side, survived.

findings.claim: 08.07 states the provenance grade is immutable after delivery while simultaneously defining a third grade that is only reachable by a post-delivery Producer acceptance. Both statements are unmarked; an implementer must invent whether the grade is a write-once field or an upgrade-only ladder.
findings.evidence: 08.07-overdub-mode.md:269 — '| Request has no live monitor and the Producer later wants the higher grade | Not retrofittable. A witness is only available while the pass happens ... | The grade is fixed at delivery. Offered *before* the pass, not after. |' CONTRADICTED BY 08.07-overdub-mode.md:176 — '| **Counter-attested** | The Producer accepted the pass into the project. | Acceptance is signed and attributable (08.05.04 D-01).' and 08.07-overdub-mode.md:290 — '| Accepted | Producer accepted a pass | Counter-attested. Handed to 07 as a project asset, to 08.05.04 as a graded record, to 02 as evidence.' and 08.07-overdub-mode.md:264 — 'Record stands at `delivered-by`, unaccepted.' The domain CX takes the opposite side of the same question: realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-cx.md:150 — 'attendance row written at the *delivered* grade. If a live witness attended (CX-09), grade upgrades. No rollback; grade only ever rises on evidence.'
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the provenance grade field is sealed at delivery (making `counter-attested` unreachable) or mutable upward on later evidence (making 'fixed at delivery' false). This is the domain's thesis-bearing output, consumed by domain 02's tier model.
findings.twoImplementerTest: Implementer A reads line 269 and seals grade at delivery, so acceptance never changes it. Implementer B reads lines 176/290 and CX-07 and implements an upgrade-only ladder that rises at acceptance. Both are faithful to the text and produce different records for the same session.

findings.claim: What the shared click does when latency drifts mid-take is explicitly named as an unresolved product choice, with no owner, no decision, and a deferral target (/ideate-discover Step 5) that the tree elsewhere records as already completed. No open question in 08.01.03, the 08.01 index, or the domain index covers it.
findings.evidence: 08.01.03-shared-clock-click-countin.md:56 — '| Latency drifts during a take, breaking alignment | `[PENDING — Step 5]` — whether the click re-aligns live (which itself is an audible timing change) or holds and lets it drift. Both are bad; this is a genuine product choice. | `[PENDING]` |'. The stage it defers to is complete: 08.01.03-shared-clock-click-countin.md:99 and :100 both say 'Re-pointed from the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5', and realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-index.md:132 records 'MoSCoW has since run'. The file's own three questions cover different ground: Q-01 'Symmetric or conductor — which model does the product commit to' (:98), Q-02 conductor drop-out succession (:99), Q-03 whether the click is recorded as an alignment reference (:100).
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an in-flight click re-aligns to changing directional delay (producing an audible timing change under the performers' hands, which 08.01.03 D-02 forbids for the timing model) or holds and accumulates drift, and if it re-aligns, what the trigger threshold is.
findings.twoImplementerTest: Implementer A re-aligns continuously and shifts musicians' time mid-bar. Implementer B holds the click and lets the ensemble drift apart. The file states both are bad and picks neither.

findings.claim: Overdub round-trip calibration is described as a gate in two places and as explicitly not-a-gate in two others, with no marker reconciling them.
findings.evidence: 08.07-overdub-mode.md:240 — 'Calibration is a pre-flight gate item; residual + uncertainty shown per pass.' and realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-cx.md:199 — 'Mode = overdub → run overdub checklist (disk, sample rate, monitoring path, round-trip calibration) → overdub proceeds. Skip reachability/uplink. Sync gate before tracking.' CONTRADICTED BY 08.07-overdub-mode.md:280 — '| Pre-flight | Bed local | Overdub checklist: disk, sample rate, monitoring path, round-trip calibration. Not a gate (08.06 D-05) — but a skipped calibration is stated, never blank. |' and 08.07-overdub-mode.md:365 D-16 — 'Consistent with 08.06 D-05: it informs and records; it does not block.' and 08.06-session-preflight-rig-readiness.md:113 D-05 — 'Pre-flight informs and records; it does not block.'
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a player who skips or fails round-trip calibration can begin recording passes. The consequence is material: an uncalibrated pass silently mis-aligns by 5-25 ms (08.07 D-05).
findings.twoImplementerTest: Preponderance favours not-a-gate (three statements to two), so a careful implementer would likely resolve it consistently — hence warning rather than blocking — but the word 'gate' appears twice unqualified.

RESCINDED BY 08.07-overdub-mode.md:353 D-04 — 'Provenance is captured without real-time transport, at a stated grade — NOT identically to a live session ... findings.twoImplementerTest: The contradiction is flagged in two sibling files, so it is not strictly silent — but the parent index was never remediated and a downstream reader following the documented entry path (index first) hits the refuted claim with no marker on it.

findings.claim: The provenance-grade enum has two different third rungs across the domain, and the domain CX attributes its version to a Deep Think annotation that does not contain it. The grade is a user-visible string and a cross-domain contract with 02.
findings.evidence: realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-cx.md:225 — '08.05.04 emits not a boolean but a *grade* (`delivered-by` < `observed-playing` < `session-captured+attested`, DT-08). 02.04.02 consumes the grade as the top rung of its tier ladder.' CONTRADICTED BY the cited DT-08's own table at 08.07-overdub-mode.md:172-176, whose three rungs are '**Delivered-by**', '**Observed-playing**' and '**Counter-attested** | The Producer accepted the pass into the project.' 08.05.04-session-attendance-provenance.md:50 uses only the first two ('A live-room segment is `observed-playing`; an overdub is `delivered-by` by default') and separately at :207 attributes 'session-captured+attested' to domain 02's ladder, not to 08's grade: "`02.04` Q-01 names 'session-captured+attested' as the top rung of its candidate ladder". The grade is rendered to users verbatim — 08.07-overdub-mode.md:258: "Grade shown honestly: 'delivered-by (single party)'."
findings.forcedInvention: The exact value set of the grade enum that 08 emits and 02 consumes, and whether `counter-attested` and `session-captured+attested` are the same rung, adjacent rungs, or one 08-side value and one 02-side value.
findings.twoImplementerTest: Implementer A models a three-value 08 grade ending in `counter-attested`. Implementer B models a three-value grade ending in `session-captured+attested` and has no representation for Producer acceptance. The cross-domain contract with 02.04.02 differs in both.

findings.claim: Whether a live session may degrade to Overdub mid-session is deferred to a stage the tree records as completed, with no owner and no re-point. No question in the domain index or in 08.07 covers it.
findings.evidence: realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-cx.md:52 — '5. **State transition conflict**: A live session degrading to overdub mid-session is plausible but likely disruptive; the local-round-trip figure overdub needs is a *different* measurement than the network verdict, so a mid-session switch is not a free reuse of state. `[Deferred — Step 5]`.' The CX file is dated 2026-07-18 (:6) and Step 5 is recorded complete at realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-index.md:132 ('MoSCoW has since run and did not decide this (D-24: Step 5 complete)'). The domain index's seven open questions (Q-01 through Q-07, :130-136) cover classification, cross-cuts, infrastructure, keep-or-fold, the instrument-pair table, two probable merges, and recording consent — none covers mid-session mode switching. 08.07's six questions (:371-376) do not either.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the product offers a mid-session live-to-overdub transition at all, and if so whether the in-flight session's takes, attendance segments and grade carry across the boundary.

findings.claim: The upload size bound for an overdub pass is delegated to 'the request's declared scope', but nothing in the overdub request model declares a scope, size or duration. The sibling feature that solves the same problem derives its bound from an observed session, which does not exist in overdub.
findings.evidence: 08.07-overdub-mode.md:267 — '| Player delivers an implausibly large file | Accepted if it is genuinely a long multichannel pass — this is the mode where a 40-minute multitrack is legitimate. **Bounded by the request's declared scope, not by a guess.** | Progress, and a size warning against their own remaining upload, not a refusal. |'. What the request actually declares is enumerated at 08.07-overdub-mode.md:218 — 'Producer creates an overdub request against a project (07): selects the bed, chooses its fidelity ..., writes the brief, sets the deadline, marks the target section(s).' No scope, size, duration or channel-count declaration appears there, in the bed-package table (:64-71), or in D-06/D-09. Contrast the live path, where the bound is explicitly derived: 08.05.01-local-first-multitrack-capture.md:259 — 'The expected size is *known* from the observed session (duration × channels × format). A file materially beyond the envelope is rejected before it consumes storage.'
findings.forcedInvention: What 'the request's declared scope' is — whether the target sections imply a maximum duration, whether channel count is bounded, and therefore what size triggers the warning versus a rejection.

findings.claim: 'Witness' names two structurally different artifacts inside one sub-domain — a server-side retained copy of what the network carried, and an endpoint-local pre-talkback recording of the inbound mix — and 08.05.01 offers its server-side version as a candidate answer to 08.05.02's reference question, which 08.05.02's own governing mechanism rules out.
findings.evidence: Server-side sense, 08.05.01-local-first-multitrack-capture.md:304 DT-06 — 'The platform already carried a degraded copy of every participant's audio; correlating an uploaded local take against what the network heard proves the take is the take', and :362 Q-05 — 'Does the platform retain a witness copy of what the network carried, and for how long? ... and a candidate answer to 08.05.02 Q-01.' Endpoint-local sense, 08.05.02-take-alignment-drift-correction.md:72 — '| **R2** | **Timing witness correlation** — each endpoint's local, pre-talkback recording of the inbound ensemble mix' and :109 — 'If a pre-talkback tap is not available at an endpoint, that endpoint has **no witness**, not a compromised one.' The two cannot be the same artifact: 08.05.02:64-67 establishes 'Alignment places a track by comparing it to a reference **that the endpoint's own clock recorded**. This is the mechanism: when the endpoint records the reference, the reference's *apparent duration in that file* directly reveals the endpoint's rate error' — a server-held copy has no such property. Retention also conflicts: 08.05.02-take-alignment-drift-correction.md:301 D-08 — 'The timing witness is a measurement artifact ... and is discarded at seal', versus 08.05.01 Q-05 treating retention as open.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the session produces one witness recording or two, where each lives, who consents to each, and which one (if either) can serve alignment. The consent surface differs sharply: 08.05.02 Q-05 (:321) and 08.05.01 Q-03 (:360) both flag witness recording as a live consent problem, and an implementer conflating the two under-scopes it.

findings.claim: The retrospective highlight window is the feature's central mechanism but its duration is never stated, and unlike every sibling threshold in this domain it is not routed to any stage as an open number.
findings.evidence: 08.05.03-auto-highlights-moment-flagging.md:105 D-01 — '| D-01 | A flag anchors to a retrospective window ending at the gesture | Humans flag after realising. See DT-01. |' and :66 — '| Flag placed late (they realised after it happened) | The normal case, not an edge case. ... | Flag creates a region ending at the gesture, not starting there. |'. DT-01 (:88) mentions the idiom without adopting a value — 'why "capture the last 30 seconds" is the standard idiom for this problem' — and no decision or question fixes one. The file's three questions are flag privacy (:115), audio analysis scope (:116) and the note/flag merge (:117). Contrast how the tree handles every other threshold of this class: 08.06-session-preflight-rig-readiness.md:122 Q-03 (staleness window), 08.05.02-take-alignment-drift-correction.md:322 Q-06 ('the 1 ms / 5 ms / 20 ms confidence-tier boundaries'), 08.01.02-playability-verdict-tempo-ceiling.md:103 Q-01 (instrument-pair thresholds) — all explicitly routed to /create-prd-compile as 'a threshold with a cost on both sides'.
findings.forcedInvention: How much audio a single flag gesture captures. The file states DT-01's failure mode is that 'getting this backwards makes it useless in a way that is not obvious until someone tries to use it' — a window too short misses the take it was meant to keep, one too long makes every flag the same region.
